summary.intent: Autonomously run the full post-execute-phase ship loop for GSD phase 73 (verify, secure, crypto/privacy review, security review, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit CLI review, ship, resolve PR reviews) without babysitting, per the Ship Phase playbook.
summary.outcome: Verification/security/validation all passed (7/7 verified, 17/17 threats closed, 0 gaps), diagnosed and fixed a local TEE-worker stack misconfiguration blocking 3 SDK E2E tests, fixed a genuine stale test assertion (Test 20) and a real CodeRabbit MAJOR finding in useSharedNavigationActions.ts, got SDK E2E to 106/106 green, and committed the fixes as three scoped commits — ship/PR steps had not yet run by end of transcript.

repo: Local dev stack: cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing claims host port 3001, pushing cipherbox-tee-worker's container port 3001 to remap onto host 3002 — but TeeService defaults TEE_WORKER_URL to http://localhost:3001, so it silently talks to the wrong container.

The API (via TeeKeyStateService), not the TEE worker itself, populates the tee_key_state DB table by fetching the worker's pubkey at boot; if that fetch fails (wrong port or bad auth), the table stays empty and all tombstone/republish e2e tests fail with 'tee_key_state is empty'.

apps/tee-worker/src/middleware/auth.ts gates /public-key (and other endpoints) behind Authorization: Bearer $TEE_WORKER_SECRET — a host-run API must be given the worker container's matching secret or it gets a 401.
Phase 73 commits were already conventional (fix(73-08):, test(73-01):) — the filter-branch reword step in the playbook is not always needed; check commit subjects before blindly rewriting history.

createAndPublishIpnsRecord's SC4 change makes it catch the 410 and return {success:false, tombstoned:true} instead of throwing; resolveIpnsRecord still throws on 410 (only 404 maps to null) so only the publish half of tombstone tests needed updating.

The established pattern for re-resolving stale shared-folder state before a key operation is: seed from cache, then call getSdkClient().refreshSharedFolder(shareId) in a try/catch-ignored block (see restoreToBreadcrumbIndex at useSharedNavigationActions.ts:608) — refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey was missing this step.

code.finding: restoreToBreadcrumbIndex correctly re-resolves via getSdkClient().refreshSharedFolder(currentShareId) before reseeding publishedNode; refreshCurrentDepthWriteKey lacked this and was reseeding from the same stale in-memory getSharedFolderState(), so 'Refresh access' after a tombstone-caused write failure could never recover — fixed to mirror the established pattern.

Test 20 (WRITE-04, tombstone → publish returns 410) asserted the pre-SC4 throw-on-410 contract via expect(publishError).toBeDefined(); updated to assert the new return-value {success:false, tombstoned:true} contract since createAndPublishIpnsRecord now swallows the 410 by design.

New publishedParent resolve path uses raw resolvePublishedNode, bypassing the ROT-07 gate applied to sibling reads elsewhere in the same PR — flagged as non-blocking LOW by both the crypto/privacy and secure-phase audits, in-domain but not fixed in this session (still open).

publishNodeFn is the only production caller reaching a 410-tombstone (co-writer shared-write path) and correctly handles the new tombstoned return value, confirming the SC4 swallow-and-return contract change is safe by design.

workflow: When a background command's exit code appears masked by a pipe (e.g. reported completed/exit 0 but actual exit was 1), re-check the raw exit status directly rather than trusting the task-notification summary.

Before treating an E2E failure as pre-existing infra noise, verify per-test which code path it touches — one of three 'TEE infra' failures (Test 20) was actually caused by the phase's own contract change, not the TEE-stack gap; blanket-classifying all 3 as infra would have hidden a real stale-test bug.

Before fixing a test that no longer matches new behavior, search production callers to confirm no code still relies on the old contract — only then is 'update the test' safe rather than 'the code has a bug'.

Independent read-only analysis passes (audits, Nyquist validation, security sweep) can be launched as parallel background agents while the orchestrator does other prep work (docker/build checks) concurrently.

friction: SDK E2E gate initially showed 3 failures that looked uniformly like TEE-infra noise, requiring multi-step root-causing (container status, DB state, port mapping, auth secret) to separate genuine infra gaps (2 tests) from a real stale-assertion bug (Test 20).

The API does not log handled 4xx reasons, and diagnosing the TEE worker 404-then-401 chain required manually probing ports 3001 vs 3002 and correlating with API startup logs rather than getting a clear error from the test failure itself.

Playbook's default assumption (reword commits to conventional before shipping) didn't match reality — commits were already conventional, requiring a manual check to avoid unnecessary/risky filter-branch history rewriting.
CodeRabbit CLI surfaced 2 nits referencing hallucinated/nonexistent phase numbers (45–55/79–88), adding noise that had to be identified and discarded rather than acted on.
